findings.title: AssignmentSource.to_dict() puts a non-JSON-serializable datetime into the Celery task payload
findings.body: `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes `assignment_source.to_dict()` as a kwarg to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`. `to_dict()` is `dataclasses.asdict(self)`, which includes `queued` as a raw `datetime` object. Celery's default task serializer is JSON (and Sentry's task payloads are generally expected to be JSON-safe), and a `datetime` is not JSON-serializable, so `apply_async` will raise `TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` at enqueue time. This failure occurs synchronously inside `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign` whenever an assignment was triggered by an inbound integration webhook (which is exactly the new code path that always sets an `AssignmentSource`), so every inbound-triggered assignment would 500 the webhook handler and never enqueue any outbound sync. Even with an encoder that coerces datetimes to ISO strings, `from_dict` would then produce `queued` as a string rather than a datetime. The `queued` value should be serialized explicitly (e.g. `isoformat()` / timestamp) and parsed back in `from_dict`, or dropped from the payload. Note the new tests run tasks eagerly via `self.tasks()`, so no real serialization round-trip is exercised and this would not be caught by CI.

findings.title: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class definition time
findings.body: In a dataclass, a plain default expression is evaluated once when the class body executes, not per instance. `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` therefore freezes `queued` to the module import time for every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit value, instead of recording when the assignment was queued. Dataclasses only reject list/dict/set defaults, so this fails silently. The fix is `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The field is currently unused, so the impact is limited to incorrect data, but it is a latent bug for any future consumer of the timestamp.

findings.title: New task kwarg is not backward compatible with workers running the previous code
findings.body: `sync_assignee_outbound` now accepts `assignment_source_dict`, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` immediately starts enqueuing messages containing that kwarg. During a rolling deploy (or a rollback), a worker still running the old function signature `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` will receive these messages and raise `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict'`; after the configured retries the assignee sync is lost. The standard mitigation is to stop passing the new kwarg until the new task signature is fully deployed (or guard it behind a feature/rollout), since the parameter was given a default only on the consumer side, which doesn't protect old consumers from new messages.
